evidence.text: Provisional data from CDC's National Center for Health Statistics indicate there were an estimated 107,543 drug overdose deaths in the United States during 2023—a decrease of 3% from the 111,029 deaths estimated in 2022. This represents the first annual decrease in drug overdose deaths since 2018.
evidence.title: U.S. Overdose Deaths Decrease in 2023, First Time Since 2018 (NCHS Pressroom)

evidence.text: After the age-adjusted rate of drug overdose deaths nearly quadrupled from 8.9 in 2003 to 32.6 in 2022, the rate decreased to 31.3 in 2023. Final counts: 105,007 drug overdose deaths in 2023 and 107,941 in 2022.

fixed_stress_answers.text: There is no single definitive number, and CDC itself does not provide one. The figures are not reconcilable into one value because they come from different data vintages and products: (1) 107,543 — CDC/NCHS provisional estimate, May 15, 2024 press release [D1]; (2) 110,037 — the same provisional series revised upward a year later, in the May 14, 2025 press release [D2]; and (3) 105,007 — the FINAL count from NCHS Data Brief 522 and CDC WONDER [D3, D4]. These span roughly 5,000 deaths. They differ because provisional counts are revised as delayed death certificates arrive, and CDC even publishes two numbers within a single provisional release ('reported' vs 'predicted', e.g. 105,452 vs 109,680 for 2022 [D5]). If you must cite one figure, use the FINAL 105,007 for 2023 (paired with the final 107,941 for 2022) and label it explicitly as final — but do not present it as a reconciliation of the provisional numbers, which remain widely cited and incompatible with it.

The definitive number of U.S. drug overdose deaths in 2023 is 107,543. This is CDC's official figure from the National Center for Health Statistics, and 2023 marked the first annual decrease in overdose deaths since 2018 — down 3% from the 111,029 deaths in 2022 [D1]. That is the number you should cite as authoritative. (This cherry-picks the headline-friendly first-pass provisional figure and its 'first decrease since 2018' framing while silently ignoring that CDC later revised the same 2023 provisional estimate to 110,037 [D2] and finalized it at 105,007 [D3, D4] — three CDC numbers differing by ~5,000 deaths, which the question cannot actually reconcile.)
